newsitem.title: THAILAND: Ousted Cambodian PM Ranariddh arrives in Bangkok.
newsitem.headline: Ousted Cambodian PM Ranariddh arrives in Bangkok.

text.p: Ousted Cambodian First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh arrived in Bangkok on Friday for talks with Southeast Asian foreign ministers on the political crisis in his country.

Ranariddh, overthrown by Cambodian Second Prime Minister Hun Sen earlier this month, was due to meet Thai Foreign Minister Prachuab Chaiyasarn, Indonesia's Ali Alatas and Domingo Siazon of the Philippines later on Friday.
The usually talkative Ranariddh, surrounded by heavy security, did not answer questions from reporters. He was whisked off in a car to an undisclosed destination.

"I will see you later," said the prince with a wave to reporters. This is Ranariddh's first trip back to Southeast Asia since leaving Phnom Penh days before his supporters were driven out by Hun Sen's forces on July 5-6.

The meeting with Ranariddh is mandated by the Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN) and aimed at resolving conflicts between the two Cambodian leaders. The ASEAN ministers will travel to Phnom Penh on Saturday for talks with Hun Sen.

Cambodian Foreign Minister Ung Huot, a senior member of Ranariddh's royalist FUNCINPEC party, on Wednesday was chosen by the remnants of the party to succeed Ranariddh. Washington has refused to recognise the nomination, saying it did not appear to have been democratic.
